items.definition:
sharpness or keenness of thought, vision, or hearing
His visual acuity was excellent.

a person who studies or collects antiques or antiquities
The antiquarian spent hours examining the ancient manuscript.

the simultaneous buying and selling of securities, currency, or commodities in different markets or in derivative forms in order to take advantage of differing prices for the same asset
He made a profit through currency arbitrage.

a person who practices severe self-discipline and abstention
The monk lived an ascetic life in the monastery.

the reduction of the force, effect, or value of something
The attenuation of the signal was due to the long cable.

the electronic equipment used in aviation
He studied avionics to become an aircraft engineer.

the ultimate reality in Hinduism; a member of the highest Hindu caste
In Hinduism, Brahman is the supreme spirit.

a member of the highest Hindu caste, that of the priesthood
He was born into a Brahmin family.

a division of a long poem
Dante's Inferno is divided into thirty-four cantos.

a private meeting
The cardinals held a conclave to elect the new Pope.

feelings of anxiety or dismay, typically at something unexpected
To her consternation, the train was delayed by several hours.

a benevolent or malevolent spiritual being; a computer program that runs in the background
In Greek mythology, a daemon was a divine power or spirit.

a pair of equal and opposite electric charges or magnetic poles separated by a small distance.
The antenna functions as an electric dipole.

the act of dissipating or dispersing; wasteful expenditure or consumption.
The dissipation of energy is a key concept in thermodynamics.

the quality of being characterized by vigorous activity and progress.
The city's dynamism is evident in its rapid growth.

a sculpture or model of a person.
Protesters burned an effigy of the dictator.

the scientific study of insects.
His passion for insects led him to study entomology.

an ordinary or typical person.
He portrays the struggles of the everyman in his novels.

a person who hunts with trained falcons.
The falconer demonstrated how to handle the bird.

a nominal leader or head without real power.
The king was merely a figurehead, with real power held by the parliament.

an artificial channel for water, typically used for conveying logs or for the power it provides.
The logs were transported down the mountain using a water flume.

a Muslim who has completed the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca
The old haji shared stories of his journey to Mecca.

the act of collapsing inward violently
The old building was brought down by controlled implosion.

the action of making or becoming more intense
There has been an intensification of efforts to combat climate change.

a low storey between two main storeys of a building
The theatre has a small mezzanine level with extra seating.

A large single upright block of stone; a large, impersonal, and immovable organization
The ancient monument was a towering monolith, carved from a single piece of rock.

Potassium carbonate, especially as used in agriculture
Farmers often use potash as a fertilizer to improve crop yields.

A formal or authoritative announcement or declaration
The judge's pronouncement brought the long trial to an end.

The theory or practice of shielding a country's domestic industries from foreign competition by taxing imports
The government's new trade policy was criticized as a move towards protectionism.

A medical establishment for long-term illness
He spent several months in the sanatorium recovering from his illness.

Excessive tenderness, sadness, or nostalgia
Her sentimentality often led her to cry during sad movies.

A secondary or subordinate type
This virus has several different subtypes.

trifecta
Winning the lottery, getting a promotion, and buying a new house was a personal trifecta for him.

urology
He made an appointment with a specialist in urology.

vignette
The play was composed of several short vignettes.

whitewash
The report was accused of being a whitewash, hiding the truth.

abdication
The king's abdication shocked the nation.

the state of having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas
She felt a strong sense of ambivalence about the job offer.

a part that is joined to something larger
A tail is an appendage found on many animals.

a botanical garden devoted to trees
We spent the afternoon walking through the arboretum.

a formal reading of a criminal charge in court
The suspect's arraignment is scheduled for next week.

a contemptible or foolish person (vulgar slang)
He called me an arsehole after I cut him off in traffic.

a grooved ring holding a watch crystal or gemstone
The watch had a thin gold bezel around its face.

a bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate
His bravado masked his inner fear.

the quality of being open and honest
Her candor was refreshing, even if her opinions were sometimes blunt.

fat deposits causing dimpled skin
Many cosmetic products claim to reduce the appearance of cellulite.

a compound involved in energy production in muscles
Many athletes take creatine supplements to improve performance.

contemptuous ridicule or mockery
His proposal was met with derision from the committee members.

a competitive equestrian sport
She trains her horse for dressage competitions.

an infection of the intestines
The soldiers suffered from dysentery during the campaign.

a vehicle for carrying a coffin
The hearse slowly drove away from the funeral home.

unexpected or gratuitous benefit; spiritual nourishment
The unexpected donation was like manna from heaven for the struggling charity.

military equipment and supplies
The army's materiel was insufficient for the long campaign.

a small world or universe
The village was a microcosm of the entire country.

a large number or variety
The multiplicity of factors made the problem difficult to solve.

a surgeon specializing in the nervous system
The neurosurgeon performed a delicate brain operation.

a fence of pointed wooden stakes
The fort was protected by a strong wooden palisade.

the quality of being selective
The selectivity of the admissions process makes it very competitive.

the transfer of something for publication or broadcast by different media organizations
The TV show entered syndication after its original run.

a state of being in someone's power or having great power over someone
She was held in thrall by his captivating performance.

valley or dry riverbed
The explorers navigated through the dry wadi.

an organic compound derived from ammonia
Many important biological compounds contain amine groups.

the action or process of appeasing; pacification
The policy of appeasement failed to prevent the war.

structure with a view
From the belvedere, we could see the entire city.
